name: Het HEM
known: Founded by Amerborgh, which owns the building (hethem.nl blog, 17 June 2024).

name: Tjibaou Cultural Centre (ADCK)
known: Operating budget: about 400 million CFP francs in 2026, with 40 employees; the interim director, Weniko Ihage, described a financial recovery after several difficult years (Les Nouvelles Calédoniennes, 13 February 2026, via dnc.nc).

name: Artspace Aotearoa
known: Founded in 1987 by artists and arts workers, with Mary-Louise Browne as first director.
A charitable trust (Artspace Aotearoa Trust, charity CC20321): the Tiaki Board of Trustees, chaired by Philip M.
Clarke, appoints the Kaitohu Director, Ruth Buchanan for 2022 to 2027.

name: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
Te Uru Waitakere Contemporary Gallery
known: Andrew Clifford was the inaugural director from 2013 and left in 2023 to lead the Sarjeant Gallery (Wikipedia).
Board: Pamela Peters is chairperson since 21 September 2025, with Tosswell Grumley as treasurer and Claudia Jowitt as secretary (New Zealand Charities Register).

name: Christchurch Art Gallery
known: Blair Jackson has been director since 2018.

name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
known: Cam McCracken has been director since 2012 (Wikipedia).

name: The Dowse Art Museum
known: Renamed the Dowse Art Museum in 1981 under director James Mack (the museum's own history).

name: Govett-Brewster / Len Lye Centre
known: Named for its founder, Monica Brewster, born Govett (Wikipedia).

name: Enjoy Contemporary Art Space
known: Wikipedia names the founders as the artists Ciaran Begley, Ros Cameron and Rachel Smithies, working in a first-floor space at 174 Cuba Street until 2006.

name: Te Papa
known: Board: chair Christopher Swasbrook (appointed 5 May 2025) and deputy chair Jackie Lloyd (annual report 2024-25).

name: Toi Māori Aotearoa
known: Founded in 1996: the trust deed is dated 14 October 1996 and the trust was set up by the chairs of eight national Māori art form committees, who elect the trustees (Annual Report 2024).
It was publicly launched at "Patua: Māori Arts in Action", curated by Sandy Adsett at City Gallery Wellington (Toi Māori website).
Current trustees listed there: Tracey Morgan (Chair), Robert Gabel (Deputy Chair), Ranui Ngarimu, Sir Derek Lardelli, Lady Rose Gould-Lardelli, Rongomaiaia Te Whaiti and Reweti Arapere.
